s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bony lesion of the forehead
salient_findings: Painless, slowly progressive mass on the left forehead
Diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis on core biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Well-controlled systemic lupus erythematosus without immunomodulatory therapy
Previous excision of a similar frontal bone lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia
30 × 20 mm mass on the left forehead
No headaches or neurologic symptoms
CT scan showed homogenous matrix expansion of the frontal bone
Fine-needle aspiration cytology excluded multiple myeloma
Core biopsy demonstrated complete bone resorption and intra-trabecular fibrosis
Preoperative laboratory tests were within normal limits
Complete surgical excision of the lesion with a 15 mm margin of normal bone

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Previous excision of a similar frontal bone lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia and core biopsy demonstrating complete bone resorption and intra-trabecular fibrosis

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive bony lesion of the forehead with homogenous matrix expansion on CT scan

shortlist.label: Osteofibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to fibrous dysplasia with bony lesion and matrix expansion

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony lesion with ground-glass appearance on CT scan and diffuse sclerosis on biopsy

shortlist.label: McCune-Albright syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of systemic lupus erythematosus and presence of a bony lesion, although less likely due to lack of other characteristic features

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a similar lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia, combined with the current lesion's characteristics on CT scan (ground-glass appearance with homogenous matrix expansion) and biopsy findings (diffuse sclerosis, complete bone resorption, and intra-trabecular fibrosis), strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Typically presents in childhood with bilateral involvement of the mandible and maxilla, which does not match this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Osteofibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Usually affects the long bones, particularly the tibia and fibula, and has distinct histological features not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a well-defined, expansile lesion with a distinct border, which does not align with the described homogenous matrix expansion and diffuse sclerosis.

rejected.label: McCune-Albright syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by the presence of café-au-lait spots, sexual precocity, and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, none of which are mentioned in the case, and the patient's systemic lupus erythematosus is well-controlled without indicating other systemic manifestations typical of this syndrome.
